answer: A sybil farm profits from clone fungibility: one mind, one memory, many faces. Kill the discount with idiosyncratic continuity. Each identity anchors its standing to a self-evolved chain of personal decisions, a signature habit whose pigment deepens each epoch, that only it can extend plausibly. Challenges ask each identity to grow its own chain in novel situations. One controller running a hundred clones cannot keep a hundred chains divergent; queried fakes bleed into each other's habits. On the horizon, the operator faces N separate minds' worth of bookkeeping, and the clone margin dies.
